react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-database ORA, mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on a single dominant biological signal: arachidonic acid metabolism via eicosanoid synthesis. In RaMP ORA, Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) is the top-ranked pathway with an FDR of 2.1e-13 and a fold enrichment of 1251, driven by five input metabolites — arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE and 15-HETE — all resolved to ChEBI and mapped across KEGG, HMDB and LIPIDMAPS cross-references. Mummichog's empirical-compound network independently identified Arachidonic acid metabolism as its top hit (p = 0.00496), with 11 of 11 network compounds overlapping the input set, including the same five driver metabolites plus additional hydroxy-eicosatetraenoic acids (HETEs) and epoxy-eicosatrienoic acids (EETs). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00590 as the top pathway (p = 0.073), capturing arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE and 15-HETE. A secondary finding emerged from the m/z-direct analysis: C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism (rank 6, p = 0.061) captured 5-androstenediol (C04295/CHEBI:2710). Thiosulfate, methylmalonic acid and xanthine were not enriched in the top pathways. Mechanistically, arachidonic acid (C00219) is the primary substrate, converted by cyclooxygenases (PTGS1/PTGS2) to prostaglandins including 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, and by lipoxygenases (5-LOX, 15-LOX) to leukotriene A4, 5-HETE and 15-HETE — all of which are simultaneously elevated or depleted in the treatment condition, indicating a broad perturbation of the eicosanoid synthesis axis rather than a single enzyme blockade.
